podcast.title: Full-Time Recording and Touring Outfit
podcast.body: A Perfect Circle was formed by Maynard James Keenan as a brand new, full-time recording and touring outfit, securing a contract with a completely different record label. Keenan's commitments to this band immersed him in recording, which in turn delayed the creation of Tool's third album. "Mayor joined what appeared to be a brand new, full-time recording and touring outfit, with a contract with a completely different label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Maynard James Keenan's Family Winemaking Heritage
podcast.body: Maynard James Keenan, known for his work in Tool, A Perfect Circle, and Puscifer, has a family history in winemaking, with relatives in northern Italy who he believes still make wines. This heritage influenced his own venture into viticulture. "His family still might make wines in northern Italy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars – Maynard James Keenan's Arizona Wine Operations
podcast.body: Maynard James Keenan owns Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars, high-end wine operations located in the Sedona area of Arizona, specifically in Cornville, north of Phoenix and south of Flagstaff off I-17. He invested money earned from Tool and A Perfect Circle into these ventures. Merkin refers to a wig worn in the pubic region, while Caduceus, the ancient symbol for commerce, is associated with the brand's website, www.cadocious.org. His wines, particularly the '84 cab blend, have received excellent reviews, and the tasting center invites wine lovers to sample and purchase. "Maynard owns Merckin Vineyards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Project History (1995-2004)
xref.body: This project was created in 1995 and involved Trent Reznor, Atticus Ross, and a variety of friends, continuing off and on for nine years. Despite the collaboration, nothing was ever officially released. "I already mentioned the tapeworm project, which was created in 1995 and included a lot of different friends. They were continued off and on for nine years, but nothing was ever released."

xref.title: Desert Session Projects – Produced by Eleven Members
xref.body: Josh Homme's Desert Session projects received production assistance from Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider of the band Eleven, following their work on Chris Cornell's solo album. This collaboration brought Johannes and Schneider into contact with members from various other prominent bands, including A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects, which brought them into contact with members of a perfect circle, nine-inch nails, Danzig, Wade, Maryland Manson's band, and PJ Harvey."

xref.title: Guitar Tech for Tool, Co-founded A Perfect Circle
xref.body: Billy Howerdel initially worked as a guitar tech for the band Tool. During Tool's downtime, he co-founded A Perfect Circle, a band that features Tool's lead singer, Maynard James Keenan. "Billy Howardale was a guitar tech for tool. When they weren't doing anything he played in a perfect circle featuring tool singer Maynard James Keenan."

xref.title: Producers for Chris Cornell's Solo Album – Launchpad for Other Gigs
xref.body: The group Eleven, comprising Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider, played a crucial role in producing Chris Cornell's debut solo record, *Euphoria Morning*. Their work on this album garnered them further producing gigs for notable artists like No Doubt and Josh Homme's Desert Session projects, connecting them to members of A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "Chris reliant on both of them to help produce his debut solo record Euphoria Morning... who, based on this work, got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Survival of Tracks as "Tapeworm DNA"
xref.body: Despite the Tapeworm album never being officially released, two tracks are noted to carry its "DNA": "Passive" on A Perfect Circle's 2004 album "Emotive" (a descendant of a song called "Vacant"), and "Potions" which appeared on a Puscifer album. These releases offer glimpses into the material created during the project. "Two release tracks do have tapeworm DNA, though. One is called passive. It's on a perfect circle's 2004 album, Emotive. It's a descendant from a song called Vacant. Another is Potions, which appeared on a pusifer album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
